node.label: Richard Hofstadter
node.date_label: Social Darwinism in American Thought (1944) · The American Political Tradition (1948) · The Age of Reform (1955)
node.description: A historian of American political culture whose interpretations moved from economic-interest explanations toward ideas, status anxieties and political irrationality. Eric Foner’s retrospective distinguishes his critical account of consensus from celebratory consensus history and also identifies its limits.

proposed_edges.relationship: Critically reworks the economic-conflict interpretation and explores ideological consensus in American politics.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Foner distinguishes Hofstadter’s critical consensus interpretation from celebratory versions and notes the later reconsideration of conflict.

proposed_edges.relationship: Brings status anxiety, symbols and irrationality into accounts of political culture.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Foner’s named substantive reading also judges the treatment of Populists and Progressives exaggerated and elitist in important respects. This qualification survives the contribution arrow.
